claim: Genetic interaction screens have aided our understanding of complex genetic traits, diseases, and biological pathways.
source: Genetic interaction screens have aided our understanding of complex genetic traits, diseases, and biological pathways.
evidence: This is a general statement about the utility of genetic interaction screens, supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Approaches for synthetic genetic analysis with null-alleles in metazoans have not been feasible.
source: However, approaches for synthetic genetic analysis with null-alleles in metazoans have not been feasible.
evidence: This statement is supported by the context of the manuscript describing the novelty of their approach and the limitations of prior methods.

claim: The authors present a CRISPR/Cas9-based Synthetic Genetic Interaction (CRISPR-SGI) approach enabling systematic double-mutant generation.
source: Here, we present a CRISPR/Cas9-based Synthetic Genetic Interaction (CRISPR-SGI) approach enabling systematic double-mutant generation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The CRISPR-SGI technique was applied in Caenorhabditis elegans.
source: Applying this technique in Caenorhabditis elegans, we comprehensively screened interactions within a set of 14 conserved RNA binding protein genes, generating all possible single and double mutants.
evidence: This describes the experimental system used in the study.

claim: The authors comprehensively screened interactions within a set of 14 conserved RNA binding protein genes.
source: Applying this technique in Caenorhabditis elegans, we comprehensively screened interactions within a set of 14 conserved RNA binding protein genes, generating all possible single and double mutants.
evidence: This describes the scope of the genetic screen performed.

claim: All possible single and double mutants were generated for the 14 RNA binding protein genes.
source: Applying this technique in Caenorhabditis elegans, we comprehensively screened interactions within a set of 14 conserved RNA binding protein genes, generating all possible single and double mutants.
evidence: This describes the completeness of the mutant collection.

claim: Many double mutants displayed fitness defects, revealing synthetic interactions.
source: Many double mutants displayed fitness defects, revealing synthetic interactions.
evidence: This is a summary of the phenotypic results from the screen.

claim: Double mutants of mbl-1 and exc-7 displayed a severely shortened lifespan.
source: For one interaction between the MBNL1/2 ortholog mbl-1 and the ELAVL ortholog exc-7, double mutants displayed a severely shortened lifespan.
evidence: This describes a specific phenotype observed in the double mutant.

claim: mbl-1 is the MBNL1/2 ortholog in C. elegans.
source: For one interaction between the MBNL1/2 ortholog mbl-1 and the ELAVL ortholog exc-7, double mutants displayed a severely shortened lifespan.
evidence: This identifies the mammalian homolog of the C. elegans gene.

claim: exc-7 is the ELAVL ortholog in C. elegans.
source: For one interaction between the MBNL1/2 ortholog mbl-1 and the ELAVL ortholog exc-7, double mutants displayed a severely shortened lifespan.
evidence: This identifies the mammalian homolog of the C. elegans gene.

claim: Both exc-7 and mbl-1 are required for regulating hundreds of transcripts and isoforms.
source: Both genes are required for regulating hundreds of transcripts and isoforms, and both may play a critical role in lifespan extension through insulin signaling.
evidence: This is supported by the RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: exc-7 and mbl-1 may play a critical role in lifespan extension through insulin signaling.
source: Both genes are required for regulating hundreds of transcripts and isoforms, and both may play a critical role in lifespan extension through insulin signaling.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on epistasis experiments with daf-2.

claim: CRISPR-SGI reveals a rich genetic interaction landscape between RNA binding proteins in maintaining organismal health.
source: Thus, CRISPR-SGI reveals a rich genetic interaction landscape between RNA binding proteins in maintaining organismal health, and will serve as a paradigm applicable to other biological questions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the data presented in the study.

claim: CRISPR-SGI will serve as a paradigm applicable to other biological questions.
source: Thus, CRISPR-SGI reveals a rich genetic interaction landscape between RNA binding proteins in maintaining organismal health, and will serve as a paradigm applicable to other biological questions.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the future applicability of the method.

claim: RNA binding proteins are critical regulators of all aspects of RNA metabolism.
source: RNA binding proteins are critical regulators of all aspects of RNA metabolism, and have been implicated in human health and disease (Castello et al., 2013; Gerstberger et al., 2014a; Lukong et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: RNA binding proteins have been implicated in human health and disease.
source: RNA binding proteins are critical regulators of all aspects of RNA metabolism, and have been implicated in human health and disease (Castello et al., 2013; Gerstberger et al., 2014a; Lukong et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Specific combinations of RNA binding proteins are important for tissue-specific regulation of RNA processing and abundance.
source: A number of studies have demonstrated the importance of specific combinations of RNA binding proteins for tissue-specific regulation of RNA processing and abundance (Brooks et al., 2015; Chen and Manley, 2009; Elkon et al., 2013; Schoenberg and Maquat, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Hundreds of metazoan RNA binding proteins have no described molecular or cellular function.
source: However, despite their importance in regulating many facets of gene expression, hundreds of metazoan RNA binding proteins have no described molecular or cellular function (Castello et al., 2013; Gerstberger et al., 2014b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The challenge in characterizing RNA binding proteins may be due to redundancy in their regulation of shared RNA targets.
source: Part of the challenge in characterizing these factors may be due to redundancy in their regulation of shared RNA targets.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the lack of characterized functions.

claim: Genetic analyses in multicellular animals have been limited to ablating RNA binding protein genes in isolation.
source: For practical reasons, genetic analyses in multicellular animals have been limited to ablating RNA binding protein genes in isolation (Barberan-Soler et al., 2011) or studying a single genetic interaction by targeting two members of the same family (Gehman et al., 2012; Ule et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing the limitations of previous approaches.

claim: Deletion of multiple RNA binding protein genes with overlapping functions should reveal stronger 'synthetic' phenotypes relative to the loss of individual factors.
source: On the other hand, deletion of multiple RNA binding protein genes with overlapping functions should reveal stronger 'synthetic' phenotypes relative to the loss of individual factors, and shed light on the role of these genes in animal development and physiology.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that motivated the study.

claim: The synthetic genetic array (SGA) approach in budding yeast and bacteria has revealed widespread synthetic interactions between genes.
source: In budding yeast and bacteria, the development of such systematic pairwise gene deletion schemes, including the synthetic genetic array (SGA) approach, have revealed widespread synthetic interactions between genes, in which double mutant phenotypes differ from what would be expected given observed single mutant phenotypes (Butland et al., 2008; Costanzo et al., 2010; Schuldiner et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on SGA in yeast and bacteria.

claim: Analogous genetic strategies to SGA in multicellular organisms have not been feasible.
source: However, analogous genetic strategies in multicellular organisms have not been feasible.
evidence: This statement establishes the novelty of the current work by highlighting the gap in existing methods.

claim: RNAi triggered by feeding has been used as a tool for analyzing genetic interactions in C. elegans.
source: In C. elegans, RNA interference (RNAi) triggered by feeding animals double-stranded RNA has been used as a tool for analyzing genetic interactions, either by subjecting loss of function mutants to RNAi by feeding, or by targeting two genes simultaneously by RNAi (Baugh et al., 2005; Byrne et al., 2007; Dixon et al., 2009; Lehner et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on RNAi-based genetic interaction studies.

claim: The use of RNAi in genetic interaction studies can be limited since gene activity is knocked down rather than knocked out.
source: However, despite its throughput, the use of RNAi in genetic interaction studies can be limited since gene activity is knocked down rather than knocked out (Kamath and Ahringer, 2003), complicating the interpretation of synthetic phenotypes.
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing the limitations of RNAi.

claim: Neurons are generally refractory to RNAi by feeding.
source: Additionally, neurons are generally refractory to RNAi by feeding, unless specific hypersensitive genetic backgrounds are used which often have negative effects on animal physiology(Asikainen et al., 2005; Calixto et al., 2010; Firnhaber and Hammarlund, 2013; Sieburth et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on neuronal RNAi resistance.

claim: The CRISPR-SGI strategy employs the CRISPR-associated enzyme Cas9 to generate double-strand DNA breaks in the genome.
source: This strategy employs the CRISPR-associated enzyme Cas9 to generate double-strand DNA breaks in the genome (Dickinson and Goldstein, 2016; Norris et al., 2015).
evidence: This describes the molecular mechanism of the CRISPR-SGI approach, supported by citations.

claim: Following cleavage of chromosomal DNA by Cas9 and a single guide RNA, animals are created carrying marked deletion alleles through homology-directed gene replacement of a target gene with a heterologous GFP transgene.
source: Following cleavage of chromosomal DNA by Cas9 and a single guide RNA (sgRNA), animals are created carrying marked deletion alleles through homology-directed gene replacement of a target gene with a heterologous GFP transgene.
evidence: This describes the gene replacement strategy used in the study.

claim: Reporter fluorescence can be followed as a proxy for the gene deletion.
source: Thus, reporter fluorescence can be followed as a proxy for the gene deletion (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes how the GFP marker is used to track deletions, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: To make an array of double mutants, a collection of genes are independently replaced with two compatible non-overlapping tissue-specific GFP reporters.
source: To make an array of double mutants, a collection of genes are independently replaced with two compatible non-overlapping tissue-specific GFP reporters, and then crossed to generate double heterozygous F1 progeny (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the strategy for creating double mutants, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Homozygous double mutants are isolated by microscopy.
source: These animals are allowed to self-fertilize and generate F2 animals, and homozygous double mutants are isolated by microscopy.
evidence: This describes the method for identifying double mutants.

claim: The CRISPR-SGI strategy eliminates the need for laborious large-scale PCR and/or sequencing to ascertain the genotype of the animal at each generation.
source: This strategy for creating double mutants provides a substantial increase in throughput as it eliminates the need for laborious large-scale PCR and/or sequencing to ascertain the genotype of the animal at each generation.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the CRISPR-SGI approach.

claim: The 14 RNA binding protein genes studied have expression in the nervous system.
source: Using this technique, we focused on generating deletions in a set of 14 evolutionarily conserved RNA binding protein genes with expression in the nervous system, reasoning that RNA binding proteins co-expressed in the same tissue are more likely to exhibit synthetic phenotypes.
evidence: This describes the selection criteria for the genes studied.

claim: RNA binding proteins co-expressed in the same tissue are more likely to exhibit synthetic phenotypes.
source: Using this technique, we focused on generating deletions in a set of 14 evolutionarily conserved RNA binding protein genes with expression in the nervous system, reasoning that RNA binding proteins co-expressed in the same tissue are more likely to exhibit synthetic phenotypes.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that guided the gene selection.

claim: The 14 RNA binding protein genes were selected by combining expression data from previously published studies with tissue-specific RNA sequencing.
source: These genes were selected by combining expression data from previously published studies with tissue-specific RNA sequencing we performed (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This describes the data sources used for gene selection.

claim: The list of 14 genes includes RNA binding proteins with well-known roles in the nervous system and other tissues, as well as factors with little or no known phenotype or function.
source: This list includes RNA binding proteins with well-known roles in the nervous system and other tissues, as well as factors with little or no known phenotype or function.
evidence: This describes the diversity of the genes selected for study.

claim: Deletions marked by GFP repair transgenes were created in all 14 genes.
source: We created deletions marked by GFP repair transgenes in all 14 genes.
evidence: This describes the mutant collection generated.

claim: Resulting phenotypes were consistent with previous literature, including two genes with strong neuronal phenotypes (unc-75/CELF and mec-8/RBPMS2).
source: Resulting phenotypes were consistent with previous literature, including two genes with strong neuronal phenotypes (unc-75/CELF and mec-8/RBPMS2) (Brenner, 1974; Chalfie and Sulston, 1981; Lundquist and Herman, 1994) and one with a mild non-neuronal phenotype (exc-7/ELAVL)(Fujita et al., 2003) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This validates the mutants by comparing to known phenotypes, supported by citations and figure reference.

claim: exc-7/ELAVL has a mild non-neuronal phenotype.
source: Resulting phenotypes were consistent with previous literature, including two genes with strong neuronal phenotypes (unc-75/CELF and mec-8/RBPMS2) (Brenner, 1974; Chalfie and Sulston, 1981; Lundquist and Herman, 1994) and one with a mild non-neuronal phenotype (exc-7/ELAVL)(Fujita et al., 2003) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes a known phenotype, supported by citation and figure reference.

claim: A competition assay was designed in which equal numbers of mutant and wild-type animals were placed on the same growth plate and allowed to grow for two generations.
source: To test for more subtle fitness defects, we took advantage of the fact that our mutants are labeled with GFP and designed a competition assay in which equal numbers of mutant and wild-type animals were placed on the same growth plate and allowed to grow for two generations.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the fitness assay.

claim: The fraction of GFP-positive worms on the plate at the end of the assay reflects the multi-generational competitive fitness of the mutant worms relative to wild-type worms.
source: The fraction of GFP-positive worms on the plate at the end of the assay reflects the multi-generational competitive fitness of the mutant worms relative to wild-type worms (Figure 2A and see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes how fitness is measured in the competition assay, with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: The majority of deletions had little or no effect on fitness.
source: Performing the competition assay on single mutants revealed that while the majority of deletions had little or no effect on fitness, there were a few deletions causing substantial defects (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a result from the competition assay, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A few deletions caused substantial fitness defects.
source: Performing the competition assay on single mutants revealed that while the majority of deletions had little or no effect on fitness, there were a few deletions causing substantial defects (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a result from the competition assay, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: unc-75 and mec-8 mutations cause serious organismal phenotypes.
source: These included unc-75 and mec-8, mutations in which are known to cause serious organismal phenotypes as described above (Figure 2—figure supplement 1) (Brenner, 1974; Chalfie and Sulston, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citations and figure reference showing known phenotypes.

claim: Disruption of C25A1.4 led to significant defects in fitness.
source: Surprisingly, however, we also found that disruption of two genes, C25A1.4 and the RBM24 ortholog sup-12, also led to significant defects in fitness.
evidence: This is a novel finding from the competition assay.

claim: Disruption of sup-12 led to significant defects in fitness.
source: Surprisingly, however, we also found that disruption of two genes, C25A1.4 and the RBM24 ortholog sup-12, also led to significant defects in fitness.
evidence: This is a novel finding from the competition assay.

claim: sup-12 is the RBM24 ortholog in C. elegans.
source: Surprisingly, however, we also found that disruption of two genes, C25A1.4 and the RBM24 ortholog sup-12, also led to significant defects in fitness.
evidence: This identifies the mammalian homolog of the C. elegans gene.

claim: Previous genetic studies had identified alleles of sup-12 with no obvious visible phenotypes.
source: Interestingly, previous genetic studies had identified alleles of sup-12 with no obvious visible phenotypes (Anyanful et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The sup-12 fitness defects can be partially attributed to reduced growth rate, larval lethality and reduced fertility.
source: Upon further analysis, we found that the sup-12 fitness defects can be partially attributed to reduced growth rate, larval lethality and reduced fertility (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The sup-12 phenotypes were corroborated by a previously-unstudied sup-12(ok1843) deletion allele.
source: Importantly, these phenotypes were corroborated by a previously-unstudied sup-12(ok1843) deletion allele generated by the C. elegans knockout consortium (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This validates the findings using an independent allele, shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The CRISPR deletion of sup-12 reveals the true null sup-12 phenotype, while previously-studied missense and splice-site alleles were partial loss-of-function alleles.
source: We therefore believe that our deletion reveals the true null sup-12 phenotype, while the previously-studied missense and splice-site alleles were partial loss-of-function alleles.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of phenotypes between different alleles.

claim: All possible pairwise combinations of double mutants were generated for thirteen of the fourteen mutants.
source: Having created all single deletion mutants, we next generated all possible pairwise combinations of double mutants for thirteen of the fourteen mutants (sup-12 was excluded due to difficulty in obtaining viable homozygous lines), for a total of 78 double mutants, representing the largest targeted collection of metazoan double mutants created in a single study to date (Figure 3A).
evidence: This describes the scope of the double mutant collection, shown in Figure 3A.

claim: sup-12 was excluded from the double mutant screen due to difficulty in obtaining viable homozygous lines.
source: Having created all single deletion mutants, we next generated all possible pairwise combinations of double mutants for thirteen of the fourteen mutants (sup-12 was excluded due to difficulty in obtaining viable homozygous lines), for a total of 78 double mutants, representing the largest targeted collection of metazoan double mutants created in a single study to date (Figure 3A).
evidence: This explains why sup-12 was not included in the double mutant analysis.

claim: A total of 78 double mutants were generated.
source: Having created all single deletion mutants, we next generated all possible pairwise combinations of double mutants for thirteen of the fourteen mutants (sup-12 was excluded due to difficulty in obtaining viable homozygous lines), for a total of 78 double mutants, representing the largest targeted collection of metazoan double mutants created in a single study to date (Figure 3A).
evidence: This quantifies the number of double mutants created.

claim: This represents the largest targeted collection of metazoan double mutants created in a single study to date.
source: Having created all single deletion mutants, we next generated all possible pairwise combinations of double mutants for thirteen of the fourteen mutants (sup-12 was excluded due to difficulty in obtaining viable homozygous lines), for a total of 78 double mutants, representing the largest targeted collection of metazoan double mutants created in a single study to date (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a claim about the scale of the study relative to prior work.

claim: mec-8; exc-7 double mutants could not be created as 100% of double homozygotes were embryonic lethal.
source: Intriguingly, one of these mutants, mec-8; exc-7, could not be created as 100% of double homozygotes were embryonic lethal, although strains homozygous for one mutation and heterozygous for the other were viable (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This describes a synthetic lethal interaction, shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Strains homozygous for one mutation and heterozygous for the other (mec-8 or exc-7) were viable.
source: Intriguingly, one of these mutants, mec-8; exc-7, could not be created as 100% of double homozygotes were embryonic lethal, although strains homozygous for one mutation and heterozygous for the other were viable (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This indicates that the lethality is specific to the double homozygous condition.

claim: Simultaneous loss of mec-8 and exc-7 RNA binding proteins leads to synthetic lethality.
source: This indicates that simultaneous loss of mec-8 and exc-7 RNA binding proteins leads to synthetic lethality.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the embryonic lethality data.

claim: The synthetic lethality of mec-8; exc-7 was confirmed using previously-published canonical null alleles.
source: We further confirmed this synthetic lethality using the previously-published canonical null alleles for mec-8 and exc-7 (Chalfie and Sulston, 1981; Fujita et al., 2003) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This validates the synthetic lethality using independent alleles, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The competition assay revealed a number of synthetic fitness effects relative to the null expectation.
source: The competition assay revealed a number of synthetic fitness effects relative to the null expectation, on a continuum from weak to strong fitness defects.
evidence: This summarizes the results of the competition assay on double mutants.

claim: 11 significant double mutant fitness effects were identified (including synthetic lethality).
source: Including the synthetic lethality result above, we identified 11 significant double mutant fitness effects (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This quantifies the number of significant genetic interactions detected, shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The detected synthetic genetic interactions involve 12 of the 13 tested RNA binding protein genes.
source: Intriguingly, our detected synthetic genetic interactions involve 12 of the 13 tested RNA binding protein genes (Figure 3B), revealing many previously unknown connections between these factors.
evidence: This describes the breadth of genetic interactions detected, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Many previously unknown connections between RNA binding protein genes were revealed.
source: Intriguingly, our detected synthetic genetic interactions involve 12 of the 13 tested RNA binding protein genes (Figure 3B), revealing many previously unknown connections between these factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the novelty of the findings.

claim: tiar-3 has only one weak genetic interaction partner.
source: Some genes, such as tiar-3, have only one weak genetic interaction partner, while others are highly connected hubs, such as exc-7, which has one synthetic lethal interaction and four other synthetic fitness interactions, meaning that 45% of tested genes had a synthetic genetic effect in combination with exc-7.
evidence: This describes the connectivity of tiar-3 in the genetic interaction network.

claim: exc-7 is a highly connected hub with one synthetic lethal interaction and four other synthetic fitness interactions.
source: Some genes, such as tiar-3, have only one weak genetic interaction partner, while others are highly connected hubs, such as exc-7, which has one synthetic lethal interaction and four other synthetic fitness interactions, meaning that 45% of tested genes had a synthetic genetic effect in combination with exc-7.
evidence: This describes the connectivity of exc-7 in the genetic interaction network.

claim: 45% of tested genes had a synthetic genetic effect in combination with exc-7.
source: Some genes, such as tiar-3, have only one weak genetic interaction partner, while others are highly connected hubs, such as exc-7, which has one synthetic lethal interaction and four other synthetic fitness interactions, meaning that 45% of tested genes had a synthetic genetic effect in combination with exc-7.
evidence: This quantifies the proportion of genes interacting with exc-7.

claim: exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants showed one of the strongest negative fitness interactions (ɛ = −0.58).
source: To explore this question we further investigated one of the strongest negative fitness interactions, found in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants (Figure 2A, ɛ = −0.58).
evidence: This quantifies the synthetic fitness effect, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A substantial proportion of exc-7; mbl-1 double mutant adults died prematurely.
source: Upon more detailed analysis of these animals, we noticed that a substantial proportion of adults died prematurely (Video 1).
evidence: This describes a phenotype observed in the double mutants, shown in Video 1.

claim: While either exc-7 or mbl-1 single mutants are healthy three days into adulthood, the majority of exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants have perished.
source: Specifically, while either exc-7 or mbl-1 single mutants are healthy three days into adulthood, the majority of exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants have perished (Figure 4A).
evidence: This describes the lifespan phenotype, shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The exc-7; mbl-1 lifespan defect can be recapitulated using independently generated deletion or premature stop mutations.
source: This defect can be recapitulated using independently generated deletion or premature stop mutations (Figure 3—figure supplement 2; Brenner, 1974; Fujita et al., 2003), and can be efficiently rescued by over-expressing either RNA binding protein in the double mutant (Figure 4A).
evidence: This validates the phenotype using independent alleles, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The exc-7; mbl-1 lifespan defect can be efficiently rescued by over-expressing either RNA binding protein in the double mutant.
source: This defect can be recapitulated using independently generated deletion or premature stop mutations (Figure 3—figure supplement 2; Brenner, 1974; Fujita et al., 2003), and can be efficiently rescued by over-expressing either RNA binding protein in the double mutant (Figure 4A).
evidence: This demonstrates that the phenotype is due to loss of these specific genes, shown in Figure 4A.

claim: EXC-7 is expressed in a number of tissues including the nervous system.
source: We found that EXC-7 is expressed in a number of tissues including the nervous system, while MBL-1 is expressed almost exclusively in the nervous system, in accord with previous reports (Figure 4B) (Fujita et al., 2003; Spilker et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the expression pattern of EXC-7, shown in Figure 4B and supported by citations.

claim: MBL-1 is expressed almost exclusively in the nervous system.
source: We found that EXC-7 is expressed in a number of tissues including the nervous system, while MBL-1 is expressed almost exclusively in the nervous system, in accord with previous reports (Figure 4B) (Fujita et al., 2003; Spilker et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the expression pattern of MBL-1, shown in Figure 4B and supported by citations.

claim: Within the nervous system, EXC-7 and MBL-1 exhibit strikingly specific patterns of co-expression.
source: Moreover, within the nervous system the two factors exhibit strikingly specific patterns of co-expression.
evidence: This describes the co-expression pattern of the two proteins.

claim: In the ventral nerve cord, both EXC-7 and MBL-1 are present in cholinergic motor neurons but neither are present in the GABAergic motor neurons.
source: For instance, in the ventral nerve cord both factors are present in cholinergic motor neurons but neither are present in the GABAergic motor neurons (Figure 4C).
evidence: This describes the specific co-expression pattern in the ventral nerve cord, shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The co-expression pattern suggests EXC-7 and MBL-1 may function together in specific neuron types to regulate partially overlapping networks of RNA targets.
source: This co-expression pattern suggests these factors may function together in specific neuron types to regulate partially overlapping networks of RNA targets.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-expression data.

claim: Differences in both steady-state mRNA abundance and alternative isoform usage were identified across the various mutants relative to wild type animals.
source: Intriguingly, we identified differences in both steady-state mRNA abundance and alternative isoform usage across the various mutants relative to wild type animals, with the most severe differences found in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants (Figure 5, Supplementary files 3 and 4).
evidence: This summarizes the RNA-seq results, shown in Figure 5.

claim: The most severe differences in mRNA abundance and isoform usage were found in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants.
source: Intriguingly, we identified differences in both steady-state mRNA abundance and alternative isoform usage across the various mutants relative to wild type animals, with the most severe differences found in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants (Figure 5, Supplementary files 3 and 4).
evidence: This describes the magnitude of molecular changes in the double mutant, shown in Figure 5.

claim: Double mutants possess nearly five times as many differentially expressed genes as exc-7 mutants relative to wild type animals (100 versus 23, respectively).
source: For instance, double mutants possess nearly five times as many differentially expressed genes as exc-7 mutants relative to wild type animals (100 versus 23, respectively, Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This quantifies the number of differentially expressed genes, shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: In more than 90% of cases, expression levels are increased relative to wild type animals in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants.
source: Additionally, we observed a strong bias in the direction of expression changes in double mutants, where in more than 90% of cases, expression levels are increased relative to wild type animals (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: This describes the directionality of expression changes, shown in Figure 5A and C.

claim: exc-7 and mbl-1 act together, either directly or indirectly, at the transcriptional or post-transcriptional level to inhibit excessive mRNA levels.
source: These results suggest that exc-7 and mbl-1 act together, either directly or indirectly, at the transcriptional or post-transcriptional level to inhibit excessive mRNA levels.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNA-seq data showing increased expression in double mutants.

claim: exc-7 and mbl-1 affected hundreds of alternative splicing events.
source: We also found that exc-7 and mbl-1 affected hundreds of alternative splicing events, many of which are annotated as being involved in lifespan regulation.
evidence: This summarizes the alternative splicing results from RNA-seq.

claim: Many of the alternative splicing events affected by exc-7 and mbl-1 are annotated as being involved in lifespan regulation.
source: We also found that exc-7 and mbl-1 affected hundreds of alternative splicing events, many of which are annotated as being involved in lifespan regulation.
evidence: This connects the molecular findings to the lifespan phenotype.

claim: A significant fraction (46%) of differentially spliced junctions controlled by exc-7 were also controlled by mbl-1.
source: Notably, a significant fraction (46%) of differentially spliced junctions controlled by exc-7 were also controlled by mbl-1 (Figure 5D, e, p<1×10−60, hypergeometric test).
evidence: This quantifies the overlap in splicing targets, shown in Figure 5D and E, with statistical significance.

claim: More than a hundred differentially spliced junctions were observed in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants that were not evident in either single mutant.
source: Moreover, more than a hundred differentially spliced junctions were observed in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants that were not evident in either single mutant (Figure 5E).
evidence: This describes synthetic splicing changes in the double mutant, shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The most common classes of differential junction usage between wild-type and exc-7; mbl-1 mutants were cassette-type exons and alternative 3' splice sites.
source: The most common classes of differential junction usage between wild-type and exc-7; mbl-1 mutants were cassette-type exons and alternative 3' splice sites, which together accounted for over 50% of differential junction usage (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This describes the types of splicing changes observed, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A.

claim: EXC-7 and MBNL1 cis-elements are enriched in the downstream intron of cassette exons undergoing increased skipping in the double mutants.
source: Importantly, we observed enrichment of EXC-7 and MBNL1 cis-elements in the downstream intron of cassette exons undergoing increased skipping in the double mutants, and enrichment in the upstream intron of cassette exons undergoing increased inclusion the double mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This describes motif enrichment analysis, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: EXC-7 and MBNL1 cis-elements are enriched in the upstream intron of cassette exons undergoing increased inclusion in the double mutants.
source: Importantly, we observed enrichment of EXC-7 and MBNL1 cis-elements in the downstream intron of cassette exons undergoing increased skipping in the double mutants, and enrichment in the upstream intron of cassette exons undergoing increased inclusion the double mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This describes motif enrichment analysis, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: EXC-7 and MBL-1 regulate a network of alternative exons by binding directly to sequences in their surrounding introns.
source: These results suggest that EXC-7 and MBL-1 regulate a network of alternative exons by binding directly to sequences in their surrounding introns.
evidence: This is an inference based on the motif enrichment data.

claim: Genes with expression changes in exc-7; mbl-1 mutants exhibited no overrepresented Gene Ontology categories.
source: Genes with expression changes in exc-7; mbl-1 mutants exhibited no overrepresented Gene Ontology categories.
evidence: This describes the result of Gene Ontology analysis on differentially expressed genes.

claim: Genes with splicing changes in the exc-7; mbl-1 mutants displayed numerous enriched Gene Ontology categories.
source: On the other hand, genes with splicing changes in the exc-7; mbl-1 mutants displayed numerous enriched Gene Ontology categories, indicating control over a diversity of important pathways (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This describes the result of Gene Ontology analysis on genes with splicing changes.

claim: Top enrichment categories for genes with splicing changes include those associated with neuronal function, development and reproduction.
source: Top enrichment categories include those associated with neuronal function, development and reproduction.
evidence: This describes the specific Gene Ontology categories enriched.

claim: The enriched Gene Ontology categories are consistent with the progressive defects observed in neuronal and reproductive function in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants.
source: This is consistent with the progressive defects observed in neuronal and reproductive function in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This connects the molecular findings to the observed phenotypes, shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: A number of splicing changes between wild-type and mutant animals in lifespan-regulating genes were confirmed via RT-PCR.
source: We confirmed a number of splicing changes between wild-type and mutant animals in lifespan-regulating genes via RT-PCR (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1), including two particularly interesting candidates.
evidence: This describes validation experiments, shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: A significant alternative splicing difference in unc-62 was validated.
source: Specifically, we validated a significant alternative splicing difference in unc-62, a Meis/Homothorax family transcription factor whose alternative isoforms have been reported to differentially regulate lifespan (Figure 5F)(Van Nostrand et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes validation of a specific splicing event, shown in Figure 5F and supported by citation.

claim: unc-62 is a Meis/Homothorax family transcription factor whose alternative isoforms have been reported to differentially regulate lifespan.
source: Specifically, we validated a significant alternative splicing difference in unc-62, a Meis/Homothorax family transcription factor whose alternative isoforms have been reported to differentially regulate lifespan (Figure 5F)(Van Nostrand et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The differential usage of a 9-nucleotide micro-exon in the unc-13/Munc13 gene was validated.
source: We also validated the differential usage of a 9-nucleotide micro-exon in the unc-13/Munc13 gene, which was strongly regulated by both mbl-1 and exc-7 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This describes validation of a specific splicing event, shown in Figure 5F.

claim: unc-13 is a well-characterized synaptic protein that has also been found to regulate lifespan.
source: Intriguingly, unc-13 is a well-characterized synaptic protein that has also been found to regulate lifespan (Muñoz and Riddle, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: mbl-1 and exc-7 coordinately modulate expression levels and a network of isoforms in genes including many responsible for governing longevity.
source: These results suggest that mbl-1 and exc-7 coordinately modulate expression levels and a network of isoforms in genes including many responsible for governing longevity.
evidence: This is a summary interpretation of the RNA-seq and validation data.

claim: Premature lethality in exc-7; mbl-1 animals is not apparent during development, but specifically in adulthood.
source: Interestingly, these assays revealed that premature lethality in exc-7; mbl-1 animals is not apparent during development, but specifically in adulthood (Figure 6A).
evidence: This describes the timing of the lifespan phenotype, shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Developmental timing is normal in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants.
source: Moreover, developmental timing is normal, and behavioral correlates of organismal health such as locomotion and pharyngeal pumping are initially normal and only begin to decline in early adulthood (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the developmental phenotype, shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Behavioral correlates of organismal health such as locomotion and pharyngeal pumping are initially normal in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants and only begin to decline in early adulthood.
source: Moreover, developmental timing is normal, and behavioral correlates of organismal health such as locomotion and pharyngeal pumping are initially normal and only begin to decline in early adulthood (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the behavioral phenotypes, shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Simultaneous loss of exc-7 and mbl-1 leads to dramatic effects on post-developmental health and longevity.
source: These results indicate that simultaneous loss of exc-7 and mbl-1 leads to dramatic effects on post-developmental health and longevity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the lifespan and behavioral data.

claim: The exc-7; mbl-1 lifespan defect is much stronger than that of the classical shortened-lifespan mutant daf-16/FOXO.
source: Indeed, the exc-7; mbl-1 lifespan defect is much stronger than in that of the classical shortened-lifespan mutant daf-16/FOXO, a conserved transcription factor and component of the insulin signaling pathway (Figure 6B) (Lin et al., 1997; Ogg et al., 1997).
evidence: This compares the magnitude of the lifespan defect to a known short-lived mutant, shown in Figure 6B and supported by citations.

claim: daf-16/FOXO is a conserved transcription factor and component of the insulin signaling pathway.
source: Indeed, the exc-7; mbl-1 lifespan defect is much stronger than in that of the classical shortened-lifespan mutant daf-16/FOXO, a conserved transcription factor and component of the insulin signaling pathway (Figure 6B) (Lin et al., 1997; Ogg et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Exogenous expression of either exc-7 or mbl-1 transgenes significantly restored lifespan in double mutants.
source: Additionally, exogenous expression of either exc-7 or mbl-1 transgenes significantly restored lifespan in double mutants (Figure 6C).
evidence: This demonstrates rescue of the lifespan phenotype, shown in Figure 6C.

claim: eat-2 mutation increases lifespan in wild-type worms.
source: Both daf-2 and eat-2 mutants increase lifespan (Kimura et al., 1997; Lakowski and Hekimi, 1998) (Figure 6D and E) and we tested whether they were able to extend lifespan in the context of exc-7 and mbl-1 loss of function.
evidence: This is supported by citations and shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: daf-2 mutation increases lifespan in wild-type worms.
source: Both daf-2 and eat-2 mutants increase lifespan (Kimura et al., 1997; Lakowski and Hekimi, 1998) (Figure 6D and E) and we tested whether they were able to extend lifespan in the context of exc-7 and mbl-1 loss of function.
evidence: This is supported by citations and shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: Mutation of eat-2 increased lifespan in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants to a degree commensurate with its effect on wild-type worms.
source: Mutation of eat-2 increased lifespan in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants to a degree commensurate with its effect on wild-type worms (Figure 6D), indicating that exc-7 and mbl-1 are not necessary for lifespan extension by caloric restriction.
evidence: This describes the result of an epistasis experiment, shown in Figure 6D.

claim: exc-7 and mbl-1 are not necessary for lifespan extension by caloric restriction.
source: Mutation of eat-2 increased lifespan in exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants to a degree commensurate with its effect on wild-type worms (Figure 6D), indicating that exc-7 and mbl-1 are not necessary for lifespan extension by caloric restriction.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the epistasis experiment with eat-2.

claim: Mutation of daf-2 failed to increase the lifespan of exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants.
source: Intriguingly however, mutation of daf-2 failed to increase the lifespan of exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants (Figure 6E), suggesting that the two RNA binding proteins may play a critical role in lifespan extension mediated by loss of insulin signaling.
evidence: This describes the result of an epistasis experiment, shown in Figure 6E.

claim: exc-7 and mbl-1 may play a critical role in lifespan extension mediated by loss of insulin signaling.
source: Intriguingly however, mutation of daf-2 failed to increase the lifespan of exc-7; mbl-1 double mutants (Figure 6E), suggesting that the two RNA binding proteins may play a critical role in lifespan extension mediated by loss of insulin signaling.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion from the epistasis experiment with daf-2.

claim: The CRISPR-SGI approach enables the efficient generation of double mutants without the need for laborious PCR or sequencing validations.
source: First, it enables the efficient generation of double mutants without the need for laborious PCR or sequencing validations.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the method.

claim: The CRISPR-SGI approach offers a significant advance in throughput for generating double knockout mutants in genetically tractable multicellular animals.
source: This offers a significant advance in throughput for generating double knockout mutants in genetically tractable multicellular animals.
evidence: This is a claim about the impact of the method.

claim: The approach creates marked fluorescent mutant animals that can be competed with non-fluorescent wild type animals to screen for relative fitness under identical environmental conditions in a high throughput manner.
source: Second, because the approach creates marked fluorescent mutant animals, these mutants can be competed with non-fluorescent wild type animals to screen for relative fitness under identical environmental conditions in a high throughput manner.
evidence: This describes another advantage of the method.

claim: Relative growth or fitness measurements in budding yeast have provided countless insights into functional connections between genetic pathways in the eukaryotic cell.
source: Although relative growth or fitness measurements appear superficial in nature, in budding yeast they have provided countless insights into functional connections between genetic pathways in the eukaryotic cell (Butland et al., 2008; Costanzo et al., 2010; Schuldiner et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on yeast genetic interactions.

claim: The competitive fitness assay will serve as a rapid screening tool to identify novel genetic interactions that can be characterized in greater detail.
source: Analogously, we speculate that our competitive fitness assay will serve as a rapid screening tool to identify novel genetic interactions that can be characterized in greater detail (see below).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the utility of the assay.

claim: This type of analysis is particularly amenable to C. elegans, due to its short generation time and hermaphroditic reproduction.
source: This type of analysis is particularly amenable to C. elegans, due to its short generation time and hermaphroditic reproduction.
evidence: This explains why C. elegans is a good model for this approach.

claim: Such analysis in longer-lived, non-hermaphroditic species should be useful, but would require considerably more effort.
source: Such analysis in longer-lived, non-hermaphroditic species should be useful, but would require considerably more effort.
evidence: This is a speculation about the applicability to other species.

claim: The CRISPR-SGI strategy will be broadly applicable to additional gene sets of interest.
source: We therefore believe our strategy will be broadly applicable to additional gene sets of interest, creating a blueprint for future synthetic interaction screens with null alleles in a multicellular animal.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the future applicability of the method.

claim: ~14% of all possible pairwise synthetic interactions resulted in a fitness change.
source: Our competitive fitness assays indicated that ~14% of all possible pairwise synthetic interactions resulted in a fitness change, and these interactions were distributed across >90% of all RNA binding protein genes tested.
evidence: This quantifies the frequency of genetic interactions detected.

claim: The genetic interactions were distributed across >90% of all RNA binding protein genes tested.
source: Our competitive fitness assays indicated that ~14% of all possible pairwise synthetic interactions resulted in a fitness change, and these interactions were distributed across >90% of all RNA binding protein genes tested.
evidence: This describes the breadth of genes involved in genetic interactions.

claim: All detected genetic interactions exacerbated defects in fitness.
source: Interestingly, all detected genetic interactions in our study exacerbated defects in fitness, suggesting a general model where the combined loss of RNA binding protein genes leads to additive and/or synergistic effects on shared target transcripts (Figure 7).
evidence: This describes the directionality of genetic interactions, shown in Figure 7.

claim: The combined loss of RNA binding protein genes leads to additive and/or synergistic effects on shared target transcripts.
source: Interestingly, all detected genetic interactions in our study exacerbated defects in fitness, suggesting a general model where the combined loss of RNA binding protein genes leads to additive and/or synergistic effects on shared target transcripts (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a model proposed to explain the genetic interactions, shown in Figure 7.

claim: The high interaction frequency represents a substantial enrichment in identified genetic interactions relative to a recent larger unbiased genetic interaction analysis reported in budding yeast.
source: This high interaction frequency represents a substantial enrichment in identified genetic interactions relative to a recent larger unbiased genetic interaction analysis reported in the budding yeast.
evidence: This compares the interaction frequency to yeast studies.

claim: The observations reveal a high degree of genetic interaction among neuronal RNA binding proteins.
source: Our observations thus reveal a high degree of genetic interaction among neuronal RNA binding proteins, and highlight the value of utilizing co-expression data in genetic interaction studies.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the findings.

claim: The competitive fitness assay is likely to miss subtler phenotypes such as mild behavioral defects.
source: Moreover, our competitive fitness assay is likely to miss subtler phenotypes such as mild behavioral defects, suggesting that the true degree of synthetic interactions among neuronal RNA binding proteins is likely to be even higher.
evidence: This is a speculation about the limitations of the assay.

claim: The true degree of synthetic interactions among neuronal RNA binding proteins is likely to be even higher than detected.
source: Moreover, our competitive fitness assay is likely to miss subtler phenotypes such as mild behavioral defects, suggesting that the true degree of synthetic interactions among neuronal RNA binding proteins is likely to be even higher.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the limitations of the assay.

claim: Mutations at additional RNA binding protein gene loci may frequently act as modifiers of the severity of neurological disorders involving RNA binding proteins.
source: More generally, our results have important implications for neurological disorders involving RNA binding proteins (Castello et al., 2013; Nussbacher et al., 2015). Specifically, our data suggest that mutations at additional RNA binding protein gene loci may frequently act as modifiers of the severity of these diseases.
evidence: This is a speculation about the implications for human disease, supported by citations.

claim: Mutations in several distinct RNA binding protein genes are associated with neurodegenerative diseases such as Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).
source: Indeed, it is well documented that mutations in several distinct RNA binding protein genes are associated with neurodegenerative diseases such as Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) (Nussbacher et al., 2015; Sreedharan et al., 2008; Vance et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on ALS.

claim: unc-75/CELF displays synthetic interactions with both tdp-1/TDP-43 and fust-1/FUS.
source: Intriguingly, our double mutant screen has identified that unc-75/CELF displays synthetic interactions with both tdp-1/TDP-43 and fust-1/FUS, two genes that have been implicated in ALS (Sreedharan et al., 2008; Vance et al., 2009).
evidence: This describes specific genetic interactions detected in the screen, with citations to ALS-related genes.

claim: tdp-1/TDP-43 and fust-1/FUS have been implicated in ALS.
source: Intriguingly, our double mutant screen has identified that unc-75/CELF displays synthetic interactions with both tdp-1/TDP-43 and fust-1/FUS, two genes that have been implicated in ALS (Sreedharan et al., 2008; Vance et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on ALS.

claim: Additional work will be required to determine the nature of the genetic interactions between unc-75/CELF and tdp-1/TDP-43 and fust-1/FUS.
source: Additional work will be required to determine the nature of these genetic interactions we have observed in C. elegans, and whether the CELF family of RNA binding proteins act as modifiers of disease state in mammalian ALS models.
evidence: This acknowledges the need for future work.

claim: It is unknown whether the CELF family of RNA binding proteins act as modifiers of disease state in mammalian ALS models.
source: Additional work will be required to determine the nature of these genetic interactions we have observed in C. elegans, and whether the CELF family of RNA binding proteins act as modifiers of disease state in mammalian ALS models.
evidence: This is a speculation about the relevance to mammalian disease.

claim: Recent evidence has emerged that the splicing factor SFA-1 is required for lifespan elongation mediated by dietary restriction in C. elegans.
source: However, recent evidence has emerged that the splicing factor SFA-1 is required for lifespan elongation mediated by dietary restriction in C. elegans (Heintz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The findings extend the phenomenon of RNA binding proteins controlling lifespan to include an additional pair of RNA binding proteins (exc-7 and mbl-1).
source: Our findings extend this phenomenon to include an additional pair of RNA binding proteins, which we currently speculate are exerting a strong influence on lifespan by possibly acting downstream of the insulin signaling pathway (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary of the findings in the context of prior work, shown in Figure 7.

claim: exc-7 and mbl-1 are currently speculated to be exerting a strong influence on lifespan by possibly acting downstream of the insulin signaling pathway.
source: Our findings extend this phenomenon to include an additional pair of RNA binding proteins, which we currently speculate are exerting a strong influence on lifespan by possibly acting downstream of the insulin signaling pathway (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the epistasis data, shown in Figure 7.

claim: Additional experiments are required to confirm the predictions of the model placing exc-7 and mbl-1 downstream of insulin signaling.
source: However, additional experiments are required to confirm the predictions of this model, including testing whether over-expression of these RNA binding proteins together have the ability to increase lifespan.
evidence: This acknowledges the need for future experiments.

claim: The results expand the spotlight on RNA binding proteins as important lifespan regulators, which until now may have gone unrecognized due to genetic redundancy and/or combinatorial control.
source: Our results expand the spotlight on RNA binding proteins as important lifespan regulators, which have until now may have gone unrecognized due to genetic redundancy and/or combinatorial control.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the implications of the findings.

claim: Two RNA binding proteins co-expressed solely in the nervous system are together responsible for an aging phenotype that affects multiple tissues coordinately.
source: It is intriguing to note that two RNA binding proteins co-expressed solely in the nervous system are together responsible for an aging phenotype that affects multiple tissues coordinately.
evidence: This is an observation about the tissue-specificity of expression versus the systemic phenotype.

claim: It remains to be determined what the causal cellular or molecular mechanisms are linking the RNA binding proteins to organismal lifespan.
source: It remains to be determined what the causal cellular or molecular mechanisms are linking the RNA binding proteins to organismal lifespan, but transcriptional profiling experiments indicate that the two factors combinatorially control hundreds of genes and isoforms, many of which are involved in mediating lifespan.
evidence: This acknowledges uncertainty about the mechanisms.

claim: Transcriptional profiling experiments indicate that exc-7 and mbl-1 combinatorially control hundreds of genes and isoforms, many of which are involved in mediating lifespan.
source: It remains to be determined what the causal cellular or molecular mechanisms are linking the RNA binding proteins to organismal lifespan, but transcriptional profiling experiments indicate that the two factors combinatorially control hundreds of genes and isoforms, many of which are involved in mediating lifespan.
evidence: This summarizes the RNA-seq findings.

claim: EXC-7 and MBL-1 co-regulate gene expression in a 'synthetic' manner wherein expression is normal in either single mutant but aberrant in the double mutant.
source: We have found that EXC-7 and MBL-1 co-regulate gene expression in a 'synthetic' manner wherein expression is normal in either single mutant but aberrant in the double mutant.
evidence: This describes a pattern of gene regulation observed in the RNA-seq data.

claim: The synthetic effects on steady state RNA levels could be the result of these factors regulating transcription or RNA stability, either through direct interactions with mRNA targets, or indirectly through the modulation of factors that control these processes.
source: It is possible that such effects on steady state RNA levels could be the result of these factors regulating transcription or RNA stability, either through direct interactions with mRNA targets, or indirectly through the modulation of factors that control these processes.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed expression changes.

claim: Both EXC-7 and MBL-1 can influence other layers of RNA metabolism, including localization and RNA stability.
source: Indeed, it has been previously reported that both of these RNA binding proteins can influence other layers of RNA metabolism, including localization and RNA stability (Simone and Keene, 2013; Wang et al., 2012, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A large number of the splicing changes are additive or cumulative in nature, wherein the double mutant splicing phenotype is reflective of each of the single mutant splicing phenotypes.
source: On the other hand, a large number of the splicing changes we observe are additive or cumulative in nature, wherein the double mutant splicing phenotype is reflective of each of the single mutant splicing phenotypes.
evidence: This describes a pattern of splicing regulation observed in the RNA-seq data.

claim: The double mutant synthetic effect on viability may be caused by synthetic effects on RNA abundance.
source: It therefore may be that the double mutant synthetic effect on viability is caused by synthetic effects on RNA abundance.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the phenotype.

claim: The synthetic phenotype may be caused by splicing events regulated additively and/or cumulatively by both factors, but only upon reaching a certain threshold of mis-splicing is a phenotype revealed.
source: Alternatively, and not mutually exclusive, the synthetic phenotype may be caused by splicing events regulated additively and/or cumulatively by both factors, but only upon reaching a certain threshold of mis-splicing is a phenotype revealed.
evidence: This is an alternative speculative explanation for the phenotype.

claim: It will be of interest to identify the key targets of EXC-7 and MBL-1 that play crucial roles in maintaining long and healthy lifespan.
source: It will be of interest to identify the key targets of EXC-7 and MBL-1 that play crucial roles in maintaining long and healthy lifespan.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.

claim: The study has developed a strategy for performing systematic genetic interaction analyses in metazoans using null alleles for the first time.
source: Collectively, we have developed a strategy for performing systematic genetic interaction analyses in metazoans using null alleles for the first time.
evidence: This is a summary of the methodological contribution.

claim: Combining the CRISPR-SGI approach with competitive fitness assays led to the discovery of a hidden layer of novel genetic interactions.
source: Combining this approach with competitive fitness assays as a phenotypic readout led us to discover a hidden layer of novel genetic interactions.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings.

claim: The results highlight the importance of studying the effects of deleting combinations of RNA binding proteins in addition to studying single gene perturbations.
source: Our results thus highlight the importance of studying the effects of deleting combinations of RNA binding proteins in addition to studying single gene perturbations, and establish a novel paradigm in which these factors govern post-developmental health and longevity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the implications of the work.

claim: The study establishes a novel paradigm in which RNA binding proteins govern post-developmental health and longevity.
source: Our results thus highlight the importance of studying the effects of deleting combinations of RNA binding proteins in addition to studying single gene perturbations, and establish a novel paradigm in which these factors govern post-developmental health and longevity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion about the biological significance of the findings.
